body_text:
A bounded function $f : [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ is *Riemann
integrable* if for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists a
partition $P$ of $[a, b]$ such that:
$$ U(f, P) - L(f, P) < \epsilon. $$ The common real value
$\sup_P L(f, P) = \inf_P U(f, P)$ is the *definite Riemann
integral* of $f$ on $[a, b]$, denoted $\int_a^b f(x) \, dx$.
